title: Shortcut Guide V2's Win long-press activation breaks FancyZones Win+Arrow window cycling
author: jrobbins-LiveData
summary: Shortcut Guide’s Windows-key hold timer can fire while FancyZones consumes Win+Arrow input, interrupting repeated zone cycling during one sustained Win hold.

status.label: Cross-module design ready
status.detail: The workflow is reproducible and recent input-hook changes identify a focused coordination boundary.

next_action.label: Design Win-hold cancellation
next_action.reason: Ensure any Win+key chord cancels hold activation even when another PowerToys hook consumes it.

judgment.rationale: The user supplied a reliable cross-module reproduction and repository history shows the new Win-hold activation path and hooks that can prevent cancellation.
evidence: On 0.101.2362 the first Win+Arrow moves a window, then Shortcut Guide appears.
Disabling Shortcut Guide restores FancyZones behavior.
Shortcut Guide Win-hold options landed in #49661 and #50000 shortly before this report.
The workflow intentionally holds Win across multiple arrow presses.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue cross-module design for timer cancellation and regression coverage; keep design_in_progress until hook coordination and tests converge.

issue_context.summary: A sustained Win key is valid for repeated FancyZones moves, but Shortcut Guide interprets the same hold as activation after the first move.
known_information: Override Windows Snap and Shortcut Guide Win-hold activation are enabled.
The first arrow move succeeds; the guide then appears and later arrows stop cycling.
Disabling Shortcut Guide is a complete workaround.
The issue is routed to Product-Shortcut Guide.
inferences: FancyZones may consume Win+Arrow before the centralized hold tracker observes the different key and cancels its timer.
The fix likely belongs at the shared pressed-key coordination boundary.
issue_context.analysis: The deterministic interaction was introduced with recent Win-hold behavior. All non-Win chords during a held Win key must cancel the long-press action across hook ordering.
initial_investigation: powertoy_module.cpp registers Shortcut Guide pressed-key actions for VK_LWIN/VK_RWIN.
centralized_kb_hook.cpp starts a 900 ms timer and cancels it when a different key reaches that hook.
ShortcutGuideModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp exposes the 900 ms hold action.
FancyZones handles Win+Arrow through its own low-level path, requiring hook-order regression tests.
Issue search found no exact duplicate.
